claims.text: W-Ta-V-Cr, potentially modified with Hf, is a candidate tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy system for fusion plasma-facing components.
The proposed tungsten-based refractory HEA can achieve low-activation behavior.
The proposed alloy can maintain high-temperature mechanical performance.
The proposed alloy can maintain irradiation resistance under fusion conditions.
Conventional refractory HEAs are commonly prepared by arc melting.
Conventionally arc-melted W-Ta-V-Cr or W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloys may contain residual activation-relevant impurities.
Laser powder bed fusion can form the proposed alloy in situ from mixed elemental powders.
Fusion plasma-facing materials must operate at temperatures of at least 1000 K under severe particle, heat, and neutron exposure.
Optimized additive manufacturing will refine the alloy microstructure.
Optimized additive manufacturing will minimize residual activation-relevant elements.
The additively manufactured alloy will form a stable single BCC phase or a similar stable phase constitution.
Reducing residual impurities will reduce the formation of long-lived radioactive isotopes during neutron irradiation.
Processing-induced control of composition and microstructure will preserve high-temperature mechanical integrity.
The additively manufactured HEA will exhibit significantly less long-lived radioactivity than a conventionally processed counterpart after neutron irradiation.
The additively manufactured HEA will maintain superior high-temperature mechanical properties relative to a conventionally processed counterpart.
Traditional tungsten-based plasma-facing materials may have higher impurity levels that increase activation.
Tungsten is a leading plasma-facing material candidate because of properties including high melting temperature, low erosion, and low tritium retention.
Refractory HEAs are promising for high-temperature nuclear applications because of their elevated-temperature mechanical properties and thermal stability.
Scalability and long-term performance under cyclic fusion loading remain unverified.
The magnitude of activation reduction and the long-term stability of the refined microstructure require experimental validation.
